doing.text: sitting in her chair at the foot of the stairs with her knitting
counting the rent book with a wet thumb

looks.text: She had a shawl over a shawl and eyes that had heard every excuse for late rent and believed one.

ask: “Where was I? Where I always am, which is in this chair.”
deflect: “I don’t keep a list of who’s sorry, only who’s paid.”
nobodyElse: Nobody else. I’d have heard the third stair.

hours.8: Eight’s when I do the rent book, and I do it here.

refuse: “That’s between me and the Sacred Heart.”
ownUp: “All right. I wasn’t in my chair. Don’t tell the lodgers.”

ties.line: He pays on the Friday, which is more than I can say for his piano.
Mrs. Hauck is a good lodger. She sews, and she doesn’t sing.
Abe Sokol sends a jug round on my birthday and I don’t ask what’s in it.

secrets.text: a drop of Sokol’s gin of an evening, which she has told the priest is cough mixture

asVictim.why: she holds the rent book, and the rent book holds half the street
asVictim.foundWith: the rent book open on her knee

doing.text: wiping a glass that was already dry
reading the racing page with his lips moving

looks.text: He had forearms like a pair of hams and a moustache that did most of his talking.

nobodyElse: That’s the lot. I’d know a new face before it got its hat off.

hours.11: Eleven I change the barrel, and the whole room tells me how to do it.

ties.line: Vitale has the back booth because somebody has to, and he pays for the soup.
Nora Rafferty is the only woman on Mott Street who can drink me under my own bar.

secrets.text: the gin comes up from the river in milk cans

asVictim.why: he knows who drinks where, and what they said
asVictim.foundWith: a bar cloth in his fist

doing.text: playing scales on the edge of the table
reading a score with his glasses pushed up

looks.text: He had long hands and a short temper, and the hands were the only part of him that was patient.

ask: “Tonight? A lesson, and then I needed a drink, which is what lessons are for.”
deflect: “I teach the piano. I don’t teach people what to do.”

hours.7: Seven is the Lipschitz boy, who plays like he’s being paid by the wrong note.

ownUp: “All right. I wasn’t where I said. I was somewhere I’m ashamed of.”

ties.line: She is a good landlady. She hates the piano, but she is a good landlady.
I owe him the rent on the studio, and he reminds me in the street.

secrets.text: he plays for a dance hall on Saturdays, which his pupils’ mothers must never hear

asVictim.why: he owes everybody on the block a little, and the little adds up

doing.text: filing her nails as if they owed her money
reading a movie magazine upside down to see if it helped

looks.text: She had the headset dent in her hair still, and a voice that said “Number, please” even when it said hello.

ask: “I’ll tell you once. I talk for a living, I don’t do it for free.”
deflect: “I connect people. What they say is their business.”
refuse: “You can hold the line, mister. I’m done.”
ownUp: “Fine. I wasn’t home. Ask the man I was with, and then forget his name.”

ties.line: Sol Sirkin bought me a bracelet once and asked for it back the next week.
The dentist fixed my tooth for nothing and never once mentioned it, which is a kind of miracle.

secrets.text: she meets a married man at Sokol’s on Thursdays

asVictim.why: she hears every call on the exchange, and somebody said too much
asVictim.foundWith: her headset still round her neck

doing.text: writing very small numbers in a very small book
eating soup without taking his hat off

looks.text: He had a pencil behind each ear, in case one of them lost.

ask: “I’ll tell you where I was, and you’ll write it down, and we’ll both be happy.”
deflect: “I take bets. I don’t take sides.”

hours.9: Nine’s when the results come in from Jamaica, and I don’t move for nine.

refuse: “I don’t think I’ll answer that one. Call it a long shot.”
ownUp: “All right, I was at a game. Ask who dealt, and keep my mother out of it.”

ties.line: Sokol lets me have the booth. I let him have a little of what crosses it.
Sirkin wrote up my mother’s building for the stairs. My mother’s building has always had those stairs.

doing.text: writing in a black notebook with the stub of a pencil

looks.text: He had the look of a man who had measured your stairs and found them wanting.

ask: “I was where a man goes when he has worked all day, which is nowhere interesting.”
deflect: “I inspect buildings. People are not my department.”
ownUp: “All right. I was not where I said. It is not a building matter.”

ties.line: Steinbach owes me the rent on that studio, and pays me in chords.
My brother married her. My brother did a lot of things without asking me.
Vitale thinks a staircase is a matter of opinion.
Miss Marchetti and I had an understanding, and then we had a misunderstanding.

doing.text: looking at her own teeth in the back of a spoon

deflect: “I pull teeth. I don’t pull confidences.”
ownUp: “Yes, all right. I lied. It was about money, which is the dull kind of lie.”
